Size a trial for a robust result

Source: R/design.R
stress_design.Rd

Simulates trials from a planned design over a grid of sample sizes and effect sizes, runs the light stress test on each (covariance, inference, covariate, weighting and leave-one-subject-out families) and reports, for every cell, the conventional power next to the robustness power: the probability that the pre-specified analysis is significant and classed robust. The deletion search and a delta-adjusted tipping grid are optional and give the expected fragility index and the shift the result can absorb. This is the design-stage use of the stress test: choose the sample size so that a true effect is expected to come out robust rather than only significant, and write the expected verdict rates into the statistical analysis plan before unblinding so that the observed verdict has a pre-registered comparison.

Usage

stress_design(
  n_per_arm,
  delta,
  n_trials = 100,
  n_visits = 4,
  sigma = 10,
  rho = 0.6,
  dropout = 0.08,
  baseline_beta = 0.5,
  covariance = "us",
  method = "Satterthwaite",
  vcov = "Asymptotic",
  alpha = 0.05,
  alternatives = c("us", "ar1h", "cs"),
  loo = TRUE,
  fragility = FALSE,
  max_k = 5,
  tipping = FALSE,
  shifts = seq(0, 2, by = 0.25),
  m = 5,
  errors = "normal",
  t_df = 3,
  hetero = 1,
  mnar = 0,
  interaction = 0,
  cores = 1L,
  seed = 1
)

# S3 method for class 'stress_design'
print(x, target = 0.8, ...)

Arguments

n_per_arm

Subjects per arm to evaluate (a vector).

delta

Treatment effects at the last visit to evaluate (a vector); include 0 to see the null.

n_trials

Trials per cell.

n_visits

Number of post-baseline visits.

sigma

Residual standard deviation at each visit.

rho

AR(1) correlation between adjacent visits.

dropout

Baseline per-visit dropout probability.

baseline_beta

Slope of the response on the baseline covariate.

covariance, method, vcov

The pre-specified analysis model, as in stress_spec().

alpha

Two-sided significance level.

alternatives

Covariance structures offered as alternatives; the pre-specified one is removed from the set.

loo

Run the leave-one-subject-out family.

fragility

Run the greedy deletion search for significance up to max_k removals (slow). Otherwise a one-subject loss of significance is read from the leave-one-out rows.

max_k

Removals allowed in the deletion search.

tipping

Run a delta-adjusted tipping grid (imputed active-arm values shifted down) and record the shift at which p crosses alpha.

shifts

Shifts for the tipping grid as multiples of delta (of sigma when delta is 0).

m

Imputations per shift.

errors

"normal" or "t" (Student t with t_df degrees of freedom, scaled to the same standard deviation: heavy tails).

t_df

Degrees of freedom for errors = "t".

hetero

Multiplier of the residual standard deviation at the last visit relative to the first (1 = homoscedastic); the SD grows linearly.

mnar

Strength of missing-not-at-random dropout: dropout after a visit depends on the value the subject would have had at the NEXT visit (0 = missing at random, as the default).

interaction

Treatment effect modification by the baseline covariate: the effect at the last visit is delta * (1 + interaction * (base - 50) / 10).

cores

Worker processes. Trials are distributed, so each trial's families run on one core.

seed

Base seed; every trial's seed is derived from it.

x

A stress_design object.

target

Robustness power to reach; the print method names the smallest sample size per arm that reaches it for each non-zero effect.

...

Ignored.

Value

A data frame of class stress_design with one row per cell: n_per_arm, delta, trials, power (proportion significant), robustness_power (significant and robust), robust_given_sig, sensitive_given_sig, fragile_given_sig, marginal_given_sig, k1_given_sig (one deletion loses significance), k_reached_given_sig and k_median (deletion search, if run), tipping_margin (median shift that crosses alpha among significant trials, as a multiple of delta or sigma) and tipping_absorbed (share of significant trials with no crossing within the grid), and max_shift_se (median largest shift in pre-specified standard errors). attr(, "trials") holds the per-trial rows and attr(, "design") the settings. plot.stress_design() draws power and robustness power against the sample size.

Details

The light family set offers the alternative covariance structures, three inference methods, the model without the baseline covariate, observed-margin weighting and, if loo = TRUE, every single-subject deletion. Deletions dominate the run time at large sample sizes; loo = FALSE gives a fast first pass whose verdicts omit the deletion family.

See also

stress_calibrate() for the verdict rates of one design at a set of planned powers; stress_sap() for the analysis-plan text.

Examples

# \donttest{
des <- stress_design(n_per_arm = c(40, 80), delta = c(0, 5), n_trials = 4, loo = FALSE)
des
#> Design stress test: 4 trials per cell, 4 visits, SD 10, AR(1) 0.6, dropout 0.08 per visit; model us / Satterthwaite / Asymptotic; alpha 0.05
#> Families: covariance, inference, covariates, weighting
#>  n_per_arm delta trials power robustness_power robust_given_sig
#>         40     0      4  0.00             0.00               NA
#>         80     0      4  0.00             0.00               NA
#>         40     5      4  0.25             0.25             1.00
#>         80     5      4  1.00             0.75             0.75
#>  sensitive_given_sig fragile_given_sig marginal_given_sig k1_given_sig
#>                   NA                NA                 NA           NA
#>                   NA                NA                 NA           NA
#>                 0.00                 0                  0            0
#>                 0.25                 0                  0            0
#>  max_shift_se
#>         0.467
#>         0.343
#>         0.231
#>         0.539
#> Effect 5: no sample size in the grid reaches robustness power 0.8 (largest 0.75 at n = 80)
# }
